title: Juventus's biggest signings
brief: Name the ten most expensive players Juventus have signed since July 2000, ranked by the guaranteed fee in euros reported at the time.
period: Transfers from July 2000 to the end of the summer 2026 window (1 September 2026). Ranked by the guaranteed fee in euros as reported at the time; add-ons are left out. A loan with an obligation to buy counts at the obligation fee.

notes.Douglas Costa: Douglas Costa is 11th, just outside: €40m to make his loan from Bayern permanent in 2018 (after a €6m loan fee).
notes.Federico Chiesa: Federico Chiesa is 11th equal, just outside: €40m obligation fee in 2022 after a two-year loan costing €10m (€50m in all).
notes.Federico Bernardeschi: Federico Bernardeschi is 11th equal, just outside: €40m from Fiorentina in 2017.
notes.Gianluigi Buffon: Gianluigi Buffon: Juventus paid 75bn lire (about €38.7m) plus Jonathan Bachini in 2001. With Bachini valued, about €52.9m (TM). Counting only the cash, he is outside the ten.
notes.Pavel Nedved: Pavel Nedved is outside the ten: about 75bn lire (€38.7m) from Lazio in 2001 per La Repubblica; other sources say €41m to 45m.
notes.Randal Kolo Muani: Randal Kolo Muani is outside the ten: €38m fixed plus €12m bonuses from PSG in 2026.
notes.Paulo Dybala: Paulo Dybala is outside the ten: €32m plus €8m from Palermo in 2015.

checks: Every fee was read from Transfermarkt's club or league record page and checked against a news report (BBC, Sky, Reuters, AP, ESPN, the Guardian, Eurosport, kicker, Calcio e Finanza, A Bola or the club's statement, as named per row in transfers.csv). Where a report splits a fee into a fixed part and add-ons, the fixed part is used, so several fees are lower than Transfermarkt's (which usually adds add-ons paid or agency costs). Where a player went the other way as part of the fee, only the cash is counted unless the clubs stated a fee for each player (Arthur and Pjanic, Cancelo and Danilo, Cillessen and Neto).
